title: Bayer to Pull Heart and Kidney Drug Kerendia from German Market

contentHtml:
New Delhi: Bayer said on Tuesday it would withdraw its heart and kidney drug Kerendia from Germany from December 15, a rare step it blamed on a reimbursement system that it said failed to adequately recognise the drug's medical value.

Germany's Federal Joint Committee, a decision-making body for the health system, said in October that Kerendia offered no added benefit over comparable treatment for certain patients with symptomatic chronic heart failure, Bayer said.

The resulting reimbursement conditions made continued marketing in Germany commercially unviable, Bayer added.

The withdrawal will not affect the drug's marketing authorisation or availability in other countries.

Nine-month sales of Kerendia, a treatment of chronic kidney disease and heart failure, rose 73% to €977 million ($1.1 billion), primarily fuelled by the United States and China.

Germany's public health insurers face $6.2 billion in additional costs if the country raises drug prices in response to pressure from US President Donald Trump, a Harvard Medical School study showed earlier this month.

Bayer had withdrawn its drug Stivarga from the German market in 2016 for similar reasons.

Source : Reuters
